questions.prompt: Why do Ghanaian farmers often grow groundnut or cowpea in rotation with maize?

questions.prompt: A soil test on a farm reads pH 4.8 and the crops grow poorly. Which treatment is most appropriate, and why?

options.label: A
options.text: Apply agricultural lime such as calcium hydroxide to raise the soil pH
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Acidic soils are corrected by liming: calcium hydroxide neutralises excess hydrogen ions and raises the pH toward the range of about 5.5 to 7 that most food crops prefer. Ammonium sulfate is acid-forming and would worsen the problem, and dilution by watering cannot remove the reserve acidity held on clay and humus particles.

options.label: B
options.text: Apply ammonium sulfate fertilizer to supply more nitrogen
options.rationale: This option reflects a common misconception; the worked explanation shows why it does not apply here.

options.label: C
options.text: Water the field continuously to dilute the acidity
options.rationale: This option reflects a common misconception; the worked explanation shows why it does not apply here.

options.label: D
options.text: Add only fresh acidic compost to feed the crops
options.rationale: This option reflects a common misconception; the worked explanation shows why it does not apply here.

questions.workedSolution: Acidic soils are corrected by liming: calcium hydroxide neutralises excess hydrogen ions and raises the pH toward the range of about 5.5 to 7 that most food crops prefer. Ammonium sulfate is acid-forming and would worsen the problem, and dilution by watering cannot remove the reserve acidity held on clay and humus particles. Therefore the correct answer is A: Apply agricultural lime such as calcium hydroxide to raise the soil pH.

questions.prompt: In a waterlogged clay soil, crop roots often die mainly because

options.label: A
options.text: the standing water makes the soil too cold for enzymes
options.rationale: This option reflects a common misconception; the worked explanation shows why it does not apply here.

options.label: B
options.text: the air spaces fill with water, so roots cannot obtain oxygen for respiration
options.rationale: This is the supported answer. Roots respire aerobically, taking oxygen from soil air spaces. When water fills those spaces, oxygen diffusion to the roots stops; the roots switch to anaerobic respiration, accumulate toxic products and die, so the shoot wilts even though water is abundant. Cold, instant humus loss and nitrogen overload are not the cause.

options.label: C
options.text: the excess water dissolves all the humus immediately
options.rationale: This option reflects a common misconception; the worked explanation shows why it does not apply here.

options.label: D
options.text: the roots absorb dangerously large amounts of nitrogen
options.rationale: This option reflects a common misconception; the worked explanation shows why it does not apply here.

questions.workedSolution: Roots respire aerobically, taking oxygen from soil air spaces. When water fills those spaces, oxygen diffusion to the roots stops; the roots switch to anaerobic respiration, accumulate toxic products and die, so the shoot wilts even though water is abundant. Cold, instant humus loss and nitrogen overload are not the cause. Therefore the correct answer is B: the air spaces fill with water, so roots cannot obtain oxygen for respiration.

questions.prompt: A school maize plot measures 40 m by 25 m. Maize is planted at a spacing of 1 m between rows and 0.5 m between plants within a row. Calculate the expected plant population on the plot.
questions.workedSolution: Area per plant = spacing between rows x spacing within a row = 1 m x 0.5 m = 0.5 square metres. Plot area = 40 m x 25 m = 1 000 square metres. Plant population = plot area / area per plant = 1 000 / 0.5 = 2 000 plants.

questions.prompt: A farmer applies one 50 kg bag of NPK 15-15-15 fertilizer to a field. Calculate the mass of nitrogen contained in the bag.
questions.workedSolution: The grade 15-15-15 means the fertilizer contains 15% nitrogen by mass. Mass of nitrogen = (15 / 100) x 50 kg = 0.15 x 50 = 7.5 kg. The same bag also contains 7.5 kg of P2O5 equivalent and 7.5 kg of K2O equivalent.

questions.prompt: A community of 400 households generates an average of 2.5 kg of refuse per household per day. Calculate the mass of refuse generated in the community per week, and the number of trips a 5-tonne truck must make per week to remove it. (1 tonne = 1 000 kg)
questions.workedSolution: Daily refuse = 400 x 2.5 kg = 1 000 kg. Weekly refuse = 1 000 kg x 7 = 7 000 kg = 7 tonnes. Number of trips = 7 / 5 = 1.4, so the truck must make 2 trips per week (a fraction of a trip still requires a full journey).

questions.prompt: A school collects 250 kg of waste every week. If 60% of the waste is organic material suitable for composting, calculate the mass of organic waste available for the school compost heap each week.
questions.workedSolution: Organic fraction = 60% of 250 kg = (60 / 100) x 250 = 0.6 x 250 = 150 kg. So 150 kg of organic waste goes to the compost heap weekly, leaving 100 kg of non-organic waste for recycling or disposal.

questions.prompt: A household in Accra produces mixed refuse every day. Describe how the household can manage its waste safely from generation to final disposal.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State two ways the household should separate its waste at source.
parts.correctAnswer: Separate biodegradable waste such as food scraps from non-biodegradable waste such as plastics, glass and metals into different covered bins; keep hazardous items such as used batteries and broken bulbs apart for special collection.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe one beneficial way of disposing of the organic fraction of the waste.
parts.correctAnswer: Compost it: place the organic waste in a pit or bin, keep it moist and turn it regularly so that micro-organisms decompose it aerobically into compost manure that can be used on a garden or farm.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State two dangers of dumping refuse into gutters instead of using a waste container.
parts.correctAnswer: Refuse blocks the gutters so rainwater cannot flow, causing flooding; the dump also breeds mosquitoes, flies and rats and can contaminate water, spreading diseases such as malaria and cholera.

questions.correctAnswer: (a) Separate biodegradable waste such as food scraps from non-biodegradable waste such as plastics, glass and metals into different covered bins; keep hazardous items such as used batteries and broken bulbs apart for special collection. (b) Compost it: place the organic waste in a pit or bin, keep it moist and turn it regularly so that micro-organisms decompose it aerobically into compost manure that can be used on a garden or farm. (c) Refuse blocks the gutters so rainwater cannot flow, causing flooding; the dump also breeds mosquitoes, flies and rats and can contaminate water, spreading diseases such as malaria and cholera.
